mcqs.q: How did survival to hospital discharge for cats given canine blood xenotransfusion compare with type-matched feline allotransfusion?
mcqs.e: The xenotransfusion group had lower survival to discharge (55%) than the allotransfusion group (73%).

mcqs.q: Acute transfusion reactions were more frequent in which group?
mcqs.e: Acute transfusion reactions were more frequent in the allotransfusion group (60%) than the xenotransfusion group (20%).

mcqs.q: What was the most common reason cited for electing canine xenotransfusion?
mcqs.e: Financial constraints were the most common reason to elect xenotransfusion (49%).

mcqs.q: What was the overall conclusion about ventral bulla osteotomy for chronic otitis media-interna in previously hoarded cats?
o: Successful in most cases but not benign and not always beneficial
Should never be attempted in shelter cats
mcqs.e: Surgery succeeded in most cases but was not benign and not always beneficial, with no useful outcome predictors identified.

mcqs.q: Which organism was most commonly cultured from affected cats?
mcqs.e: Cultures were positive for Streptococcus equi subspecies zooepidemicus in 54% of cats.

mcqs.q: How often did otitis interna fully resolve after surgery?
mcqs.e: Full resolution of otitis interna was uncommon.

mcqs.q: How did metronidazole compare with a synbiotic for clinical course in dogs with acute diarrhea?
o: No significant difference in clinical outcome (CADS index)
mcqs.e: No significant differences in CADS index, fecal consistency, or defecation frequency were seen between groups.

mcqs.q: What was the effect of metronidazole on the intestinal microbiome?
o: Negative impact (lower C. hiranonis, higher E. coli)
mcqs.e: Metronidazole lowered C. hiranonis and raised E. coli, negatively impacting the microbiome.

mcqs.q: Which treatment did the authors suggest may be preferable for acute canine diarrhea?
mcqs.e: Because metronidazole harmed the microbiome without clinical benefit, synbiotics might be the preferred option.

mcqs.q: Which treatments produced significant objective improvement in OA pain versus placebo?
o: Meloxicam and EAB-277 (green-lipped mussel plus krill oil)
mcqs.e: Both meloxicam and EAB-277 significantly improved peak vertical force and orthopedic scores versus placebo.

mcqs.q: How did Biota orientalis extract (4CYTE) compare with placebo for peak vertical force?
mcqs.e: The 4CYTE group did not differ from placebo on peak vertical force.

mcqs.q: Which topical blood product did the authors recommend to minimize impact on antibiotic susceptibility in infectious keratitis?
mcqs.e: Equine blood products had a lesser impact on antimicrobial susceptibility, so they were preferred over canine.

mcqs.q: What timing was advised between the last antibiotic eyedrop and the blood product?
o: Wait at least 15 minutes after the antibiotic
mcqs.e: Administering the blood product at least 15 minutes after the antibiotic minimizes albumin-antibiotic binding in tear film.

mcqs.q: Serum versus plasma was preferred because serum had what property?
mcqs.e: Serum showed greater direct antimicrobial effects than plasma.

mcqs.q: How did puppies fed the prebiotic fiber-fortified food grow?
o: Grew normally, as expected for their age
mcqs.e: Puppies grew and developed normally on the prebiotic-fortified food.

mcqs.q: What change in short-chain fatty acids accompanied the prebiotic fiber blend?
o: A linear increase associated with favorable digestive health
mcqs.e: Short-chain fatty acids increased linearly, associated with favorable digestive and overall health.

mcqs.q: What happened to the inflammatory cytokine interleukin-7 during feeding?
mcqs.e: Interleukin-7 decreased linearly, indicating reduced inflammation.

mcqs.q: What rapid diagnostic finding supports Malassezia dermatitis?
o: Peanut-shaped budding yeasts on direct cytology
mcqs.e: Direct cytology showing peanut-shaped budding yeasts gives a rapid, reliable diagnosis.

mcqs.q: When is systemic oral antifungal therapy indicated for Malassezia dermatitis?
o: Only in severe or refractory disease
mcqs.e: Systemic antifungals are reserved for severe or refractory disease; topical azoles are first-line.

mcqs.q: What is essential for an optimal response in Malassezia dermatitis?
o: Identifying and treating the underlying cause
mcqs.e: Identifying and treating the underlying disease (often allergy) is essential for optimal outcomes.

mcqs.q: Which joint had the highest osteoarthritis prevalence in dogs older than 8 years?
mcqs.e: The elbow had the highest OA prevalence at 57.4%.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about radiographic OA in senescent dogs?
o: It is a normal finding to be expected
It should not be considered normal
It is found in nearly all joints
mcqs.e: Since most joints were free of OA, radiographic OA should not be considered a normal finding in old dogs.

mcqs.q: What was the relationship between higher OA grade and age?
mcqs.e: There was no correlation between higher grades of OA and age.

mcqs.q: What trend in hospital-acquired acute kidney injury did the IRIS guidelines note?
o: Its prevalence appears to be increasing
mcqs.e: Recent evidence suggests the prevalence of hospital-acquired AKI is increasing in veterinary medicine.

mcqs.q: Despite therapeutic advances, what remains true of AKI outcomes in dogs and cats?
mcqs.e: Overall mortality of animals with AKI remains high despite advances such as renal replacement therapy.

mcqs.q: What was the outcome in all isoxazoline neurological cases with outcome information?
mcqs.e: In all cases with outcome information, the animals recovered.

mcqs.q: Which neurological signs were most commonly reported with isoxazoline exposure?
mcqs.e: Muscle tremors and convulsions were the most common signs in both groups.

mcqs.q: Why might isoxazoline neurological adverse effects be under-attributed?
o: They occur only at lethal doses
The delay between administration and onset can be long
mcqs.e: A long delay between administration and sign onset can cause the association to be missed.
